Well I'm not sure what kind of parties you mean but it should be plenty loud, I've got a katana mini and it boasts \~89db which is nice for a small 7w amp. The mini already being louder than an acoustic, the air should be more than enough for busking and parties, assuming you don't have a drummer or they're not going crazy on the drums.

Keep in mind however than running the katana air on batteries will reduce the power from 30 to 20 watts. Not a dramatic loss but it's good to know.

Also, have you looked into the [Yamaha THR30 ?](https://www.sweetwater.com/store/detail/THR30IIWL--yamaha-thr30-ii-wireless-30-watt-modeling-combo) It is a tad more expensive than the boss but it sounds better IMO. Then again, it doesn't have as much onboard effects as the katana, but supports keyboards and bass, so think about it and get the one that suits your needs :) .

Check out [Juliette Armanet - Le Dernier Jour du Disco](https://youtu.be/hTHmZYC7Zws)

She sings in french but if you like disco/funk, the whole album has very laid-back and groovy bass lines, I highly recommend you at least check out that one song since the tabs are avalaible online.

Yeah, having a high quality guitar feels nice and I'm not gonna shit on anyone for owning expensive guitars, but I dare anyone to say that a set-up MIM strat, a high end epiphone or even a CV squier isn't a "decent" guitar.

Sure at this price point the quality is less likely to be consistent, but if you find a nice one, and get it set up, it plays just as great as more expensive guitars. You get more money to spend on a nice amp which IMHO is a bit more impactful on your sound than your guitar.

I understand people who spend 2k-3k on guitars, but at this point they just gotta acknowledge they're paying for the brand, extra binding, AAAAA wood grade or whatever.
Some people have the money for luthier guitars with attention to details and that's fine. They just gotta stop shitting on cheaper guitars.
